- **Archive parent:** Scarab Deluxe
- **Builder:** Basic Audio
- **Catalog type:** Fuzz
- **Identity:** Silicon Tone Bender MkII-type fuzz expanded from the earlier Scarab with external Bias and Fat controls. [1][2]

- **LEVEL**
- **TONE**
- **FUZZ**
- **BIAS**
- **FAT** [1]
FAT changes the amount of low-frequency content feeding the saturation stages.

- **Primary reference:** Tone Bender MkII.
- Basic Audio explicitly describes Scarab Deluxe as a silicon Tone Bender MkII-type circuit. [1]

- **Technology:** Silicon.
- An independent Guitar Pedal X report identifies **4 × BC549B** in its documented Scarab Deluxe reference. This is retained as attributed independent evidence, not as a universal factory BOM. [3]
- Exact gain grading is not documented.

- Exact clipping-device type and part number are not documented in the reviewed reliable sources.

- **9V center-negative** operation with battery support. [1]

- **Scarab:** Earlier three-knob form.
- **Scarab Deluxe:** Adds external **Bias** and **Fat** controls. [1][2]
- The archive keeps the two names distinct.

Scarab Deluxe spans tighter, potentially gated silicon fuzz into thicker sustained sounds. Bias shifts the operating point, while Fat changes the amount of low-frequency material entering the fuzz stages. [1]

- **Identity:** High
- **Tone Bender MkII lineage:** High
- **Silicon technology:** High
- **Bias/Fat additions:** High
- **4 × BC549B observation:** Medium, independent attributed evidence
- **Exact diode:** Unknown

Full Article Read Summary Key Points Boss TB-2W Tone Bender MKII Waza Craft: As of 2026-07-13, the price was £312. 3×2N404 germanium transistors, limited run (~3,100 estimated), praised MKII texture; some resale listings reach $3,000. Curated alternatives (15 total) emphasize MKII tone, each with ≥3 controls: 10 germanium, 4 silicon, 1 Ge/Si hybrid. Notable picks and prices: Magnetic Effects Solar Bender — As of 2026-07-13, the price was £135; Reeves Electro RedDotSound — As of 2026-07-13, the price was £279; Hudson Stroll On — As of 2026-07-13, the price was c£170. Selection criteria: rich MKII breakup, bias/gain control and transistor variety. As promised, I’ve drawn up a list of suitable quality alternatives - for those who did not or were unable to snag one of the excellent Boss TB-2W 2N404 Waza Editions. I’ve already passed highly favourable opinions on said pedal, while I recognise that there weren’t nearly enough to go around for all of those who wanted one. This has resulted in ridiculous price gouging - which has long afflicted the Klon Centaur in a similar manner. For the Klon Centaur around 8,000 units were made between 1994 and 2000. And the aggregate pricing there is around $6,000 equivalent nowadays, where the original fetched just $225. For the Boss TB-2W the original price was around $349/€349/£312 - yet currently there are some on Reverb.com priced at as much as $3,000 - which is of course entirely ridiculous too. Based on my serial number I would estimate around 3,100 or so TB-2W’s were made in the end.   So obviously - however impressive the Boss TB-2W is, it’s not the only game in town as such. And I’ve sought out similarly impressive TB MKII equivalents which are every bit as appealing in their own way.   I own most of this selection - so I’m well placed to pass judgement, overall I own around 20 or so MKII style Tone Benders at various different enclosure sizes - and overwhelmingly Germanium Transistor-based of various stripes.
